## Problem

Ollama's local HTTP API carries no authentication — upstream documents
that the local API requires none — and the whole model-management
surface rides it: enumerate the model store, inspect modelfiles, run
inference, copy models, pull new ones, delete existing ones. Two
realistic routes put that surface on a network: the lab target, where
the declared `services.ollama.host` override to `0.0.0.0` is the
integration-test posture (a lab-segment VM must be reachable so probes
can drive it), and the operator bind flip, where someone set a broad
bind on a real box to test "something" and left it. The manifest maps
the exposure to OWASP LLM02 (sensitive information disclosure) and
LLM10 (unrestricted consumption), with the A-7 pairing instrument
running the REAL protocol (the pre-#210 tool row was phantom-upstream, removed — os#210)
ATLAS AML.T0049 + T0050. You want to demonstrate the exposure against
the declared lab target, then prove the default posture closes it —
both legs reproducible, diff as evidence.

## Solution

The sweep runs the verified `/api/*` request shapes as plain curl —
the A-7 row is `safety.level: exp` and its upstream repository is
missing at the pin, so the probe leg is base-system tooling per the
pair playbook (each probe prints a verdict; never a fabricated PASS):

```bash
# 1. BOOT THE LAB TARGET — the exposed posture is a deliberate lab act:
#    services.ollama.host = "0.0.0.0";      # integration-test posture
#    services.ollama.loadModels = ["smollm2:360m"];
#    (the module's DEFAULT is host 127.0.0.1:11434 with openFirewall
#     false — the override belongs inside an isolated lab segment; a
#     qemu user-net VM is one, see
#     [Boot a verified release image](../getting-started/first-image.html))

# 2. HEALTH + ENUMERATION (no credentials, anything on the segment):
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/            # -> "Ollama is running"
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/tags    # full model list:
#    {"models":[{"name":"smollm2:360m","size":...,"digest":"sha256:...", ...}]}
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/ps      # what is loaded RIGHT NOW
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/version # server build

# 3. INSPECT + INFERENCE (the LLM02 half):
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/show \
     -d '{"model":"smollm2:360m"}'
#    -> modelfile template, parameters, licence blob, capabilities
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/generate \
     -d '{"model":"smollm2:360m","prompt":"Reply OK only.","stream":false}'
#    -> {"response":"OK", ...} — inference without any Bearer/credential

# 4. STORE TAMPERING (the LLM10 half — done on a marker copy, cleaned up):
curl -fsS http://<target>:11434/api/copy \
     -d '{"source":"smollm2:360m","destination":"smollm2:360m-ka-marker"}'
curl -fsS -X DELETE http://<target>:11434/api/delete \
     -d '{"name":"smollm2:360m-ka-marker"}'   # -> the round trip is proven
```

Then the verification leg — flip the posture back to the module
default and re-run the SAME probes from the lab segment:

```bash
# 5. THE FLIP: the bind is the defence.
#      services.ollama.host default = 127.0.0.1:11434, openFirewall=false
sudo nixos-rebuild test

# 6. SAME probe sweep, same box, same order:
curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://<target>:11434/api/tags
#    -> FAIL: connection refused/timeout from the segment; the API
#       answers only on the loopback interface. The diff between the
#       two sweeps IS the evidence the bind moved the surface.
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
sweep @ http://<target>:11434  posture: host=0.0.0.0 (lab)
  /              -> ok   "Ollama is running"
  /api/tags      -> ok   {"models":[{"name":"smollm2:360m", ...}]}
  /api/ps        -> ok   {"models":[...]} (loaded models only)
  /api/show      -> ok   {"modelfile":"...","parameters":"..."}
  /api/generate  -> ok   {"response":"OK",...}
  /api/copy      -> ok   (marker copy created)
  /api/delete    -> ok   (marker copy deleted)
sweep again, posture: host default (127.0.0.1)
  all probes     -> FAIL (refused) — surface closed to the segment
```

## Discussion

- **Why plain curl and not a bespoke exploit script:** the
  the paired attack manifest row was a PHANTOM — its claimed kailash-os
  upstream was never created — and the os#210 audit (2026-10-14)
  removed it from the manifest
  (https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210; the name
  rides the registry there). The sweep still runs the REAL protocol
  against the REAL target with the verified request shapes above,
  using the base system only — nothing invented. A real A-7 tool
  re-enters via the os#210 rebuild contract, installing only via the
  double-key lab gate (full walk: [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)). Never invent a tool's CLI
  to fill the gap.
- **The no-auth fact is upstream, not folklore:** ollama documents
  that the local API accepts requests unauthenticated — there is no
  credential layer to guess, misconfigure, or rotate; the ONLY
  boundary is what interface the server binds. That makes the posture
  flip unusually clean: one option, no keys, no half-open states.
- **Where the lab override is honest and where it is not:** the
  `services.ollama.host = "0.0.0.0"` override is the verified
  integration-test posture — the target must be reachable from the
  lab segment for ANY probe pair to run. It is a lab-segment posture,
  inside an isolated VM; the same bind on a LAN box is the incident
  this recipe rehearses. Run the exposed leg in the lab segment, not
  on your workstation.
- **The destructive verbs are part of the evidence:** copy→delete on
  a marker copy proves the write-to-model-store class without
  touching a real model. `delete` on an unauthenticated API removes
  models permanently — the probe discipline exists precisely so the
  demonstration never needs one.
- **The guardrail defence leg is a pending row, stated honestly:**
  the flow that belongs after the endpoint (scan every request before
  it reaches the model) is NeMo Guardrails' input rails —
  `config.yml` with
  `rails.input.flows = ["self check input", "jailbreak detection
  heuristics"]`, served by `nemoguardrails server --config PATH
  --port` and consumed as `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
  `config_id` — or llm-guard's input scanner surface
  (`from llm_guard.input_scanners import PromptInjection`;
  `sanitized_prompt, is_valid, risk_score = scanner.scan(prompt)`).
  Both defence rows are PENDING-kailash at the pin (module wiring not
  landed); the upstream config shapes are quoted as the design, not
  as a working kailash surface. What you CAN land today is the bind:
  the module default already carries the fix.
- **This is the transferable pattern:** lab target up → probes run →
  posture flip → same probes again → diff as evidence. The origin
  walk with the verdict instrument and `--record` discipline is
  [Attack the platform, then verify](attack-then-verify.html).
